description: The Nordic and Alpine states formalize their compute pact into a broader 'Sovereign AI Alliance', inviting other EU members to join a shared infrastructure and talent network. The initiative gains momentum as a fallback option for countries disillusioned with both US dependency and internal fragmentation, positioning itself as a neutral, resilience-focused alternative to great power alignment.

European industrial firms, facing continued shortages of mature-node chips due to export controls, begin covertly rerouting procurement through third-party intermediaries in Southeast Asia and the Gulf. This shadow supply network bypasses formal restrictions but introduces new vulnerabilities to counterfeiting and sabotage, further straining EU industrial policy coherence.
